summary:
This bill, cited as the “Energy Threat Analysis Center Act of 2026,” amends section 40125(c) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18724(c)) to reauthorize and expand the Department of Energy’s Energy Sector Operational Support for Cyberresilience Program.

The amendment restructures paragraph (1) by redesignating existing subparagraphs (A) through (E) as (B) through (F), inserting a new subparagraph (A) that enumerates program purposes: strengthening collective defense, response, and resilience of the U.S. energy sector through enhanced government–industry collaboration to analyze threats, deny, disrupt, and mitigate operational impacts; exchanging classified and unclassified information; collectively analyzing threats; providing sector-wide recommendations; establishing technical infrastructure for advanced analytics, discovery, alerts, and collaboration; advancing understanding of national-security risks and vulnerabilities; and increasing the sector’s knowledge of threat-actor tactics, techniques, procedures, indicators of compromise, and capabilities. Conforming amendments strike the semicolon at the end of redesignated subparagraph (D) and insert “; and”, convert the “; and” in redesignated subparagraph (E) to a period, and strike redesignated subparagraph (F) entirely.

The bill redesignates existing paragraph (2) as paragraph (7) and inserts five new paragraphs. New paragraph (2) authorizes the Secretary to execute program activities through an “Energy Threat Analysis Center,” which may be established at one or more physical locations. New paragraph (3) specifies that the provision of assistance or information is committed to the Secretary’s sole and unreviewable discretion and creates no substantive or procedural right or benefit for any other governmental or private entity. New paragraph (4) exempts the program from the Federal Advisory Committee Act (chapter 10 of title 5, U.S.C.). New paragraph (5) deems information shared under the program to be voluntarily shared and exempt from disclosure under section 552 of title 5 (the Freedom of Information Act) and any analogous State, Tribal, or local disclosure law; it mandates withholding under section 552(b)(3)(B) of title 5 and corresponding non-federal provisions. New paragraph (6) grants the Secretary transaction authority—in addition to existing authorities—to enter into contracts, cooperative agreements, grants, and other transactions with public agencies, private organizations, and persons, and permits the Secretary to use pre-approved national-security contracting mechanisms, model partnership agreements, and expedited review procedures to minimize delays.

Finally, the redesignated paragraph (7) amends the authorization of appropriations by striking “2022 through 2026” and inserting “2027 through 2031,” thereby extending the program’s authorization for five additional fiscal years. The Act does not contain an appropriation.
